releases.title: Agent Team Starter Kit
releases.summary: A configurable generator and template set for scaffolding specialized AI agent roles around a visible GitHub Issues work queue and outcome gates.
releases.originalState: Complex work can arrive as an unstructured request with unclear ownership, hidden handoffs, and no durable record of what each specialist contributed.
releases.delivered: The public starter kit packages a Python generator, configurable persona and workflow templates, GitHub Issues and Actions patterns, and Azure Functions and Azure OpenAI integration scaffolding.
releases.outcome: The pattern is designed to make multi-agent work easier to assign, inspect, and govern while keeping the work item and its history visible to people.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: clearer ownership, inspectable handoffs, and human-visible outcome gates for multi-agent work.

capabilities: Generates configurable specialist persona and workflow files.
Uses GitHub Issues and Actions templates for a durable, visible work queue.
Provides scaffolding for Azure Functions and Azure OpenAI integration.
Includes outcome framing, validation, and human intervention patterns.

architecture.label: Issue
architecture.detail: A GitHub issue holds the request, context, and visible work state.

architecture.label: Workflow templates
architecture.detail: GitHub Actions and issue-handling templates describe routing and intervention points.

architecture.label: Generated personas
architecture.detail: Configurable specialist files scaffold bounded roles that deployers must complete and wire.

architecture.label: Human gate
architecture.detail: A person can inspect the work record and decide whether the outcome is acceptable.

guardrails: GitHub keeps the request, discussion, and resulting work visible rather than hiding them in a transient chat.
Specialist roles and outcome gates can be configured for the workflow instead of granting one agent an undefined remit.
People remain responsible for reviewing consequential outputs and deployment choices.
limitations: This is scaffolding rather than turnkey autonomy: generated personas include TODOs, the runner is a stub, and deployers must complete the domain logic and wiring.
Setup requires Python, authenticated GitHub CLI access, Azure Storage, Azure OpenAI, and secured repository permissions.
Evaluation, monitoring, cost controls, and domain-specific safety checks still need to be designed for each use.

provenance.label: Agent Team Starter Kit public repository
provenance.note: Public README, quick start, generator, workflow templates, and orchestrator source are the evidence base for this entry.

article.dek: A public starter kit uses GitHub Issues as the control surface for specialist agents, explicit handoffs, and human-reviewed outcomes.

releases.title: Customer 360 for Entities

releases.originalState: A person working in a business record can have to open multiple forms or related lists to assemble the cases, orders, entitlements, contacts, and other context needed for the next action.
releases.delivered: The public solution provides an adaptive JavaScript web resource for Dynamics 365 and Dataverse forms that retrieves and presents related entity context in one place.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to reduce context switching and make the surrounding record history easier to scan before a person chooses the next action.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: less navigation between related records and a more coherent operational view at the point of work.

capabilities: Embeds a reusable web resource in Dynamics 365 or Dataverse model-driven forms.
Presents related entity information such as cases, orders, entitlements, and contacts.
Adapts the view to the current record and available related data.
Keeps the user in the host business application while they review context.

architecture.label: Current record
architecture.detail: A model-driven form supplies the current entity and record context.

architecture.label: Web resource
architecture.detail: Client-side JavaScript initializes the adaptive experience.

architecture.label: Dataverse
architecture.detail: Approved queries retrieve related operational records.

architecture.label: User action

guardrails: The experience uses the host application's identity and Dataverse permissions rather than creating a separate authority boundary.
The component presents context; it does not replace the person's judgment or automatically commit consequential changes.

limitations: The solution requires configuration for each Dataverse schema, form, and relationship set.

releases.title: Deal to Glory
releases.summary: A single-commit hackathon MVP that visualizes a deterministic, agent-styled seller workflow from voice or text input through CRM, illustrative attainment, recognition, and simulated notification stages.
releases.originalState: A spoken seller update may need to be translated into structured CRM intent, an opportunity action, an illustrative attainment view, recognition language, and a communication payload across separate steps.
releases.delivered: The public MVP implements a sequential TypeScript pipeline with keyword-based intent extraction, a mock or configured Dataverse opportunity stage, illustrative commission and attainment calculation, recognition copy, simulated notification output, Express Server-Sent Events, and browser speech or text input.
releases.outcome: The prototype is designed to make a multi-stage seller workflow visible as one narrated sequence, not to establish autonomous AI behavior, production safety, or measured seller impact.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: a tangible visualization of how one seller update could pass through structured CRM, calculation, recognition, and notification stages.

capabilities: Accepts browser Web Speech or text input and streams stage progress with Server-Sent Events.
Uses deterministic keyword extraction rather than an external AI model for deal intent.
Runs a mock path or an optional configured Dataverse opportunity update.
Produces illustrative attainment, recognition, and simulated notification payloads.

architecture.label: Voice or text
architecture.detail: The browser captures a seller update through Web Speech or typed input.

architecture.label: Deterministic stages
architecture.detail: Sequential TypeScript stages extract intent and compose the workflow.

architecture.label: CRM and calculation
architecture.detail: A mock or configured Dataverse action is followed by illustrative attainment logic.

architecture.label: Simulated notice
architecture.detail: Recognition and notification payloads are composed, but the Teams-style send is simulated.

guardrails: The journal labels the stages deterministic and agent-styled rather than claiming five autonomous AI agents.
Attainment and commission values are illustrative rather than financial evidence.
A real Dataverse deployment should add an explicit approval gate before any mutation; the current optional write path does not provide one.
limitations: When Dataverse is configured, speech completion starts the pipeline and the opportunity stage can write without an explicit user approval gate.
The notification endpoint logs intent and returns success without sending a real Teams message, while the payload marks the channel simulated.
The server enables unrestricted CORS with no authentication middleware, and browser what-if values are inserted through innerHTML without escaping.
Date handling is hard-coded around 2026, and the repository has no LICENSE file even though package.json says MIT.

releases.summary: A private, customer-neutral pattern connecting seller and CRM context, agent assistance, approved tools, next actions, human approvals, and durable receipts.
releases.originalState: Seller context, CRM records, tool assistance, follow-up actions, approvals, and evidence can be connected without a reusable boundary between recommendation and consequential execution.
releases.delivered: The private pattern separates seller intent, approved CRM context and tools, a proposed next action, explicit human approval, and a durable receipt of what was accepted or changed.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to make sales-agent extensibility easier to review and govern while keeping consequential CRM writes with an authorized person.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: a reusable sales pattern that connects context, assistance, tools, approvals, next actions, and durable receipts without autonomous CRM writes.

capabilities: Connects seller intent to approved CRM context and tools.
Frames agent output as a proposed next action rather than an automatic change.
Requires explicit approval before consequential CRM writes.
Records a durable receipt of the approved, rejected, or edited action.

architecture.label: Seller intent
architecture.detail: A seller states the goal and remains accountable for the request.

architecture.label: CRM context and tools
architecture.detail: The pattern limits retrieval and tool use to approved business context.

architecture.label: Proposed next action
architecture.detail: Agent assistance prepares a reviewable recommendation or draft action.

architecture.label: Approval and receipt
architecture.detail: An authorized person approves, rejects, or edits the action and preserves a durable receipt.

guardrails: Tools and seller context remain allowlisted and permission-bound.
Consequential CRM writes require explicit human approval.
Durable receipts preserve what was proposed, approved, edited, or rejected.
limitations: Information-only pattern; source, implementation details, operational materials, and configured systems are not published.
This private active work is not a Microsoft product, reference architecture, or officially supported offering.
No public evidence establishes production readiness, adoption, accuracy, savings, or sales outcomes.
releases.publicBoundary: Information-only. Source and operational materials are not published.

visual.alt: Seller intent moves through approved CRM context and tools to a proposed next action, explicit approval, and a durable receipt.

releases.title: Service Agent Extensibility Pattern
releases.summary: A private, customer-neutral pattern connecting case context, knowledge and tool assistance, action proposals, approvals, evidence, and customer-owned execution.
releases.originalState: Case context, knowledge, tools, evidence, proposed resolutions, record changes, and customer communications can be connected without a clear boundary around approval and accountable execution.
releases.delivered: The private pattern separates case and customer context, approved knowledge and tools, a reviewable action proposal, supporting evidence, explicit approval, and customer-owned execution.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to make service-agent extensibility easier to inspect and reuse without autonomous case changes or customer communications.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: a reusable service pattern that connects context, knowledge, tools, evidence, approvals, and customer-owned execution without autonomous case changes or communications.

capabilities: Connects case and customer context to approved knowledge and tools.
Produces reviewable action proposals with supporting evidence.
Requires explicit approval before case changes or customer communications.
Keeps final execution with customer-owned systems and authorized people.

architecture.label: Case context
architecture.detail: A service request and bounded customer context establish the review scope.

architecture.label: Knowledge and tools
architecture.detail: Approved assistance retrieves evidence and prepares a proposed action.

architecture.label: Proposal and evidence
architecture.detail: A person reviews the recommendation, supporting evidence, and uncertainty.

architecture.label: Customer-owned execution
architecture.detail: Authorized people approve and execute any case change or communication.

guardrails: Knowledge, case context, and tools remain allowlisted and permission-bound.
No autonomous case changes or customer communications are permitted.
Evidence, uncertainty, approval, and final execution remain visible and customer-owned.
limitations: Information-only pattern; source, implementation details, operational materials, and configured systems are not published.
This private active work is not a Microsoft product, reference architecture, or officially supported offering.
No public evidence establishes production readiness, adoption, accuracy, service improvement, or customer outcomes.
releases.publicBoundary: Information-only. Source and operational materials are not published.

releases.title: Pipeline-to-Consumption Unified View
releases.summary: A private decision-support pattern connecting opportunity context, milestones, adoption signals, evidence, risks, and next actions without exposing account data or forecast claims.
releases.originalState: Opportunity context, milestones, adoption signals, evidence, risks, and follow-up can live in separate views, making it difficult to discuss whether planned work and observable signals align.
releases.delivered: The private pattern brings those high-level decision inputs into one owner-reviewed view that emphasizes evidence quality, mismatches, risks, and explicit next actions.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to support better-informed human prioritization without publishing account information, asserting forecast accuracy, or treating correlation as causation.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: one evidence-aware view connecting opportunity context, milestones, adoption signals, risks, and owner-approved next actions.

capabilities: Connects opportunity context and milestones to observable adoption signals.
Keeps evidence strength, mismatches, and risks visible.
Separates decision support from automated forecast or commitment claims.
Records owner-reviewed next actions and open questions.

architecture.label: Opportunity context
architecture.detail: A generic opportunity and milestone frame establishes the decision question.

architecture.label: Adoption signals
architecture.detail: High-level observable signals are considered without exposing account data.

architecture.label: Evidence and risk
architecture.detail: Alignment, gaps, uncertainty, and risks remain explicit.

architecture.label: Owner next action
architecture.detail: A person decides what to validate, prioritize, or follow up next.

guardrails: The view is decision support and does not automate forecasts, commitments, or external reporting.
Correlation and timing signals are not presented as causation or measured business impact.
The public description contains no account, opportunity, milestone, consumption, or forecast data.
limitations: Information-only description; source, data mappings, operational materials, and working views are not published.
This private active build is not a Microsoft product or officially supported offering.
No public evidence establishes forecast accuracy, adoption, production use, savings, ROI, or customer outcomes.
releases.publicBoundary: Information-only. Source and operational materials are not published.
